root_cause.text: In `net/rds/rdma.c::__rds_rdma_map()`, the `put_user()` error path incorrectly performed a second unpin/free of the scatterlist and user pages after `get_mr()` had already transferred ownership of those resources to the transport, causing a double cleanup/use-after-free on copy-to-user failure.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes `unpin_user_pages(pages, nr_pages);` and `kfree(sg);` from the `put_user(cookie, ...)` failure branch, and the commit message explicitly states that once `get_mr()` succeeds “__rds_rdma_map() hands sg/pages ownership to the transport” so the error path “must not free those resources again before dropping the MR reference.”

agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch removes `unpin_user_pages(pages, nr_pages);` and `kfree(sg);` from the `put_user(cookie, ...)` failure branch, and the commit message explicitly states that once `get_mr()` succeeds “__rds_rdma_map() hands sg/pages ownership to the transport” so the error path “must not free those resources again before dropping the MR reference.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the `put_user` failure path in `__rds_rdma_map` by removing incorrect cleanup before returning `-EFAULT`.
intent_record.what: In the error path after `put_user(cookie, ...)` fails, the code no longer conditionally calls `unpin_user_pages(pages, nr_pages)` and `kfree(sg)` when `need_odp` is false; it now directly sets `ret = -EFAULT` and jumps to `out`.
intent_record.how: This changes cleanup behavior on a user copy failure so that the page unpinning and scatter-gather buffer freeing are no longer performed in this specific branch, likely because that cleanup is handled elsewhere or was incorrect in this context. Runtime behavior on the failure remains returning `-EFAULT`, but resource management during that failure path is altered.

grouping_result.intent: Fix the `put_user` failure path in `__rds_rdma_map` by removing incorrect cleanup before returning `-EFAULT`.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the reported root cause: it fixes the `put_user()` failure path in `__rds_rdma_map()` by removing incorrect cleanup that would otherwise double-unpin/free resources already handed off, which is the vulnerability.

candidates.rationale: This cleanup runs on the put_user() failure path even though get_mr() has already taken ownership of the pinned pages; unpinning them again causes double cleanup and can lead to use-after-free.
This frees the scatterlist again on the copy-to-user error path after ownership was transferred, contributing to the double free/cleanup bug described in the root cause.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement performed an extra cleanup in the put_user() failure path after get_mr() had already taken ownership of the pinned pages, causing double unpin/free and potential use-after-free.
This statement freed the scatterlist again on the copy-to-user failure path after ownership had already been transferred, contributing to the double cleanup/use-after-free bug.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct described in the root cause is the double cleanup on `put_user()` failure in `__rds_rdma_map()`. In this diff, that error path already performs cleanup only once: `if (args->cookie_addr && put_user(...)) { if (!need_odp) { unpin_user_pages(pages, nr_pages); kfree(sg); } ret = -EFAULT; goto out; }`. This means the function now explicitly unpins and frees the scatterlist on the copy-to-user failure path instead of doing an extra, incorrect cleanup after ownership transfer. The earlier bug pattern (a second unpin/free after `get_mr()`/transfer) is not present here, so the vulnerable construct is absent and the fix is already in place.
